doc.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1959-05-25

title: Ragtime concerts, organ grinders and amateur night bands
summary: She describes ragtime concerts, white organ grinders, and bands at amateur night, including Robichaux and Clarence Williams.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you say that you worked, that you were on the stage around here before you went to Chicago?
Just in a ragtime, see, they didn't call it a minstrel. Minstrel, it was a ragtime concert, but you went through the same performance, you know.
I was wondering, did you know any of the organ grinders? Who they'd be?
They were all white fellas. They didn't have no colored idol. They used to have little monkeys, you know. And when they'd get ready, he'd come out with a little cup. You never heard of them?
Oh, sure, but there was one colored guy that did, and I'm trying to think of his name.

Well, I don't remember any colored, but I know these white, they used to come around and, you know, the children would save their nickels for it. And they'd get out and dance with each other. And then during that time, they had, like, they call it talent night, but amateur night, you know. And if you had a play in your backyard, you'd get out there and brush your heels out there dancing in order to get on this, you know, amateur night to see what you could do. Well, nobody instructed you. You just got out there and danced, and then if you made good, you just went from there.
Did they have a band or a piano there for when you were trying out?

Oh, yeah. This, at the Lyric, they had a Robichaux's band when they used to have amateur night at the Regal. And Clarence Williams used to have a band here. Clarence Williams, now. Yeah, yeah, he had a wife named Edith Taylor. He was a songwriter. Yeah, that's the same one. He used to have a little band here, Clarence. Sure, yeah. That was on the AMA two nights.
